parsed.explanation: The division is genuinely protective: gender-identity public-accommodations law (2014), hate-crime coverage (2021), a 2024 trans sanctuary law, court-protected bathroom/locker access, X markers on state IDs, strong care coverage. Once inside, everyday exposure is low. But the parent regime governs the traveller's journey and cannot be overridden locally: the January 2025 order imposes a birth-sex binary on documents and bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities (national buildings); the February 2025 cable directs officers to refuse cases with apparent discrepancies and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility; foreign governments have issued advisories and foreign nationals have been detained over visa issues; national custody and immigration detention document hormone removal, forced labour and sexual abuse. Two killings in ten weeks in one city carry no denominator and prove no elevated rate. Border/detention exposure, not local society, sets the ceiling: above the harshest anchors' local-only cases, materially below an independent jurisdiction with these protections.
